summary: A doubly-connected gradiometric transmon (8-mon) qubit with nano-airbridge interconnect achieves a nearly threefold enhancement in Ramsey coherence time $T_2^*$ compared to reference X-mons while preserving full electrical tunability and maintaining energy relaxation times $T_1$ in the 20–45 µs range. A spatially correlated flux-noise model reveals that the gradiometric geometry suppresses low-frequency magnetic noise through destructive interference between oppositely wound loops, with suppression factor $S(">d) \ propto (d/\xi)^2$ for long-wavelength noise.
motivation: Frequency-tunable transmon qubits suffer significant flux-noise-induced dephasing despite their advantages for individual qubit addressability and parametric gates. Existing strategies relying on material optimization and magnetic shielding do not address the fundamental sensitivity of the SQUID geometry to external flux fluctuations.
method: The 8-mon incorporates two counter-wound loops linked by a nano-airbridge to form a symmetrically balanced gradiometric SQUID, where the flux line couples preferentially to one loop. Devices were fabricated on c-plane sapphire substrates using aluminum with Dolan-bridge junctions, and coherence was characterized via Ramsey, echo, and spectroscopic measurements at 15 mK with and without $\mu$-metal shielding across three chips.
result: At small flux bias, the 8-mon achieves $T_2^* > 30$ µs (2–3× longer than X-mon values $< 15$ µs) while maintaining $T_1 \approx 30$–45 µs without echo decoupling; long-term frequency stability improved from $\approx 0.4$ MHz drift (X-mon, shielded) to $< 0.1$ MHz (8-mon) over 10 hours, and remained stable without shielding whereas unshielded X-mons drifted $> 20$ MHz.
